findings: The board chair finds the exact runner internally admissible as an evidence instrument for the ten external campaigns.
The board chair refuses to treat the runner, its qualification receipt, or synthetic fixtures as evidence that a real campaign occurred or that release standing changed.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Every real campaign, canonical ledger amendment, public release, and external-effect decision remains outside this runner admission.

findings: The creative direction review finds the object consistently classified as an operator instrument rather than a performed campaign.
The review retains all physical, human, private, provider, field, deployment, score, and release holds.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: No campaign narrative is accepted without its actual operator, venue, procedure, observations, evidence, acceptance, and failure disposition.

findings: Initialization, evidence intake, observation, status, finalization, verification, proposal, and qualification are separate executable transactions.
No transaction can directly mutate the canonical ledger or authorize release.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Usability by real campaign operators remains an external human campaign rather than a software inference.

findings: The status transaction makes missing observations, missing evidence classes, absent bytes, failed hashes, unlinked observations, and nonpassing observations explicit.
The public receipt preserves evidence identity and claim scope without retaining local source paths.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Comprehension by representative human operators remains unproved until the real human campaign is performed.

findings: The tranche makes no visual or typographic product claim.
The not-applicable gate is explicit and does not borrow finish standing from another surface.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: No visual-surface quality is evaluated by this command-line runner admission.

findings: The tranche makes no motion claim.
Operator-supplied timestamps remain evidence fields and do not manufacture temporal observation.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Real interruption, recovery, and temporal behavior remain campaign observations.

findings: Evidence custody preserves identifier, class, basename, actor, time, rights, scope, visibility, locator, byte count, and SHA-256.
Local paths and source bytes are omitted from public receipts, while optional operator-controlled readback verifies exact retained evidence.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Rights and custody outside the operator-supplied record remain accountable to the real evidence custodian.

findings: The runner can record authority, access, safety, observation, work-or-no-work, completion, and acceptance as distinct field evidence.
The runner cannot grant access, safety authority, work authority, completion, or affected-actor acceptance.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: No lawful field campaign has standing from this runner admission alone.

findings: The contract identifies the actors, devices, software, focus, semantics, announcements, magnification, reduced-motion, and task-completion evidence required for real assistive-technology work.
The qualification receipt makes no claim that assistive-technology or affected-user operation occurred.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Real assistive technologies, users, devices, browsers, and tasks remain untested until their campaign receipt exists.

findings: The runner deterministically rejects missing requirements, tampered evidence, tampered receipts, duplicate identities, symlinks, invalid timestamps, unlinked observations, nonpassing observations, and unauthorized ledger transitions.
Qualification derives actual passed and open counts from the canonical ledger rather than a hard-coded campaign state.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Performance and resilience of each real campaign venue remain outside the runner’s synthetic qualification.

findings: Public receipts reject private and credential keys, raw evidence, file content, local paths, and implied external effects even when a payload checksum is otherwise valid.
Every receipt and proposed amendment preserves false public-release and ledger-mutation authority.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Actual private-data custody, consent, deletion, provider credentials, and jurisdictional rights remain external campaigns.

findings: A passed campaign receipt can create only a separate proposed one-row ledger amendment with release-authority review required.
The canonical ledger, release HOLD, public endpoint, deployed rollback, final score, and canonical task rows remain outside runner authority.
seat_reviews.uncertainty: Every actual campaign and release decision remains dependent on its own accountable receipt and authority review.

object_classification.reason: The object is a local-first evidence runner for ten external campaigns, and its qualification explicitly does not claim that any campaign occurred or passed.

actors_and_authority.reason: Campaign operator, evidence custodian, affected actor, provider or field authority, deployment operator, release authority, and cold successor retain separate observation, acceptance, amendment, and release authority.

mechanism_fidelity.reason: The runner operates real workspace, evidence, observation, status, finalization, verification, and amendment mechanisms with hard completeness, evidence-linkage, digest, and authority gates.

source_and_authorship_custody.reason: Evidence bytes remain operator-controlled while receipts preserve file identity, class, time, actor, rights, scope, visibility, locator, byte count, digest, and evidence-manifest checksum.

interaction_semantics.reason: The command interface exposes distinct initialization, evidence, observation, status, finalization, verification, amendment, and qualification transactions with no label-only substitution.

visual_and_typographic_finish.reason: This gate is not applicable because the tranche is a command-line evidence runner and creates no visual or typographic product surface.

motion_and_temporal_continuity.reason: This gate is not applicable because campaign times are operator-supplied evidence fields and the tranche creates no motion surface.

responsive_and_accessible_operation.reason: The runner is scriptable through a standard command interface, while actual assistive-technology, human, and physical-device campaigns remain the evidence this runner is designed to collect.

performance_resilience_and_failure.reason: Missing evidence, missing observation classes, unlinked observations, tampered bytes, tampered receipts, nonpassing observations, duplicate identities, symlinks, invalid states, and unauthorized ledger transitions fail deterministically.

security_privacy_rights_and_purpose.reason: Public receipts omit local paths and source bytes, reject prohibited keys and external-effect implications, retain visibility and rights, never self-authorize release or ledger mutation, and require separate authority review.

continuity_export_rollback_and_successio.reason: Deterministic portable receipts and bounded amendments pass, while every real campaign and any remaining public endpoint, deployed rollback, or independent successor operation retain their own external evidence requirements.

qualification_receipts_and_public_effect.reason: The exact-head workflow retains the complete runner receipt while campaign-performed, physical-standing, ledger-mutation, public-release, public-effect, and constitutional-count-effect fields remain false or none.

admitted_claim: The repository may admit the exact local-first external campaign runner, its ten-class contract, deterministic evidence and observation law, strict finalization, receipt verification, bounded proposed-ledger amendment, adversarial tests, and runner qualification receipt.
holds: No assistive-technology, human, device, network, private, provider, field, archive, public-endpoint, or deployed-rollback campaign is performed by runner qualification.
No initialized workspace, synthetic fixture, complete form, green workflow, or successful process exit has physical or human standing.
No campaign receipt may enter the canonical release ledger without separate release-authority review of its source-linked evidence and proposed amendment.
Private-controlled evidence bytes remain outside Git and public artifacts; the runner qualifies only bounded metadata, rights, scope, digests, and operator-controlled readback.
No public release, deployed endpoint, production rollback, external effect, whole-product score, endorsement, or canonical task-count mutation is admitted.
The first real use of every campaign class requires its own operator, actual venue, versioned procedure, observations, evidence, acceptance, and failure disposition.

authority_receipt.decision_scope: Admit only the external campaign evidence runner and its internal qualification receipt.
prohibited_effects: insurance denial, underwriting, premium setting, coverage triage, or parcel-risk scoring
property valuation, resident ranking, eligibility, funding, enforcement, inspection, or adverse action
evacuation, safety, entry, traffic, pruning, labor, work, remediation, completion, or institutional acceptance
canonical release-ledger mutation without separate authority review
whole-product public qualification, external endorsement, 99-point score award, or canonical task-count mutation

qualification_boundary: A passing decision proves only that the runner can initialize, record, hash, validate, finalize, verify, and propose amendments under the ten-class contract. It does not prove that any real campaign occurred, that any canonical ledger row passed, or that public release standing changed.
control_question: Can an accountable operator perform one named external campaign, retain every required observation and evidence class, verify exact bytes, record acceptance and failure disposition, and produce a receipt that release authority can review without exposing private evidence or inventing physical standing?
